GDD §09 risk: sameness (Watch Dogs: Legion); briefs/010/research/df-for-the-suborned.md
Legion's bios did nothing, and DF's wiki says 'many gameplay effects of facets are still unknown'. Every field a simulated person carries names the rule that reads it, and the schema rejects a carried field with no reader. A generated fact no rule reads is trivia.

Nothing hand-authored, everything checked
No person, mission or line of dialogue is written by hand. Sky writes the rules and the generators. The simulation plays every generated mission before a player sees it.

hits.text:
people rules › mix
the culture baseline is the cast row: an area × occupation's temperament weights. No temperament may hold more than rowMaxShare of a row's weight, and a unit with whenStaffAtLeast staff or more carries at least unitMinDistinct temperaments.
row cap 60% of a row's weight; a unit of 3+ staff carries at least 2 temperaments
§09 risk: sameness (Watch Dogs: Legion); §04 Hero and Menace turn different halves of the city
DF draws each person from a culture baseline, then lets them deviate. Our baseline is the cast row, and this cap keeps every person from being the baseline. At any workplace of three or more there are two kinds of person, so there are two ways in at two prices, which serves the pillar orchestrate the city. 0.6 and 3 are [S].

people rules › positions
every work unit has exactly one keeper; the rest of its staff take the other positions of its category. A mission casts by position and place (a server on shift at the café), never by name.
